extracted.intended_audience: investigators and research staff preparing NIH R01 (renewal) grant applications, particularly biomedical/HIV prevention researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and documenting a renewal (competing continuation) NIH R01 application, including required forms, facilities & resources, human subjects information, assay validation/QA, data sharing, and subcontract/consortium agreements for a biomedical HIV prevention project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA/application format instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format. Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the current FOA-specific instructions when preparing applications; sample applications are illustrative only and may be out of date. Ensure attachments, forms, and page limits match the active FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects compliance and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Are Human Subjects Involved? If YES: Is the Project Exempt from Federal regulations? If No, indicate whether IRB review is pending or approved; include IRB Approval Date and Human Subject Assurance Number as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must declare human subjects involvement, exemption status, and provide IRB approval details or indicate pending status. Provide supporting documentation in Research & Related Other Project Information and ensure institutional assurances are in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) conformance for analytical assays
rubrics_metrics.description: The HAL applies Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) standards to meet the drug assay development requirements developed by the Food and Drug Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratories performing bioanalytical assays should demonstrate GLP conformance across equipment, personnel, methods, practices, records, and controls. Include QA roles, monitoring procedures, and evidence of GLP implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bioanalytical method validation per FDA regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods must follow FDA regulations on bioanalytical method validation; QA director monitors and inspects analytical studies to assure conformance with validation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide validation reports and show personnel expertise in method development, validation, and recognition of invalid/irregular results. Cite prior validated methods where available and describe planned validation activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPQA submission and approval of antiretroviral assays before use in NIH trials
rubrics_metrics.description: All antiretroviral assays in biomatrices must be submitted to the DAIDS-supported Clinical Pharmacology and Quality Assurance Program (CPQA) prior to running assays from studies funded by the NIH clinical trials networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include evidence of prior CPQA approvals (e.g., tenofovir/emtricitabine assays approved) and a plan/timeline to submit and obtain CPQA approval for any new assays (e.g., dapivirine, cabotegravir) before sample analysis begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data security, access control, and logging (HIPAA compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A HIPPA-compliant server is dedicated to research data storage. Access to this server is restricted to persons on the UCSF network, requires network log-on authentication, is further restricted to staff working on the project, and access to research files is logged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate HIPAA-compliant storage, authentication mechanisms, fine-grained access control, and audit logging. Describe who has access, how access is provisioned, and how logs are maintained and reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data backup and off-site redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily back-up is performed on network servers. Databases are backed up three times daily including one backup which is routed off site to magnetic storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document backup frequency, off-site/air-gapped copies, and recovery procedures. Provide evidence of routine backups and policies for data retention and restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources demonstrate institutional capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed description of institutional facilities (laboratory space, clinical clinic resources, office space, major equipment, IT infrastructure, specimen processing and storage capabilities) to support the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should list relevant core facilities, major equipment, staffed personnel, clinical space (e.g., Ward 86), and administrative/logistical support. Include how facilities meet project needs and letters of support/transfers where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed laboratory staffing and QA roles
rubrics_metrics.description: List permanent staff, research associates, QA director, laboratory director, and investigators with relevant experience (e.g., personnel devoted to method development, validation, and implementation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify roles and percent effort for staff, QA oversight responsibilities, and credentials/experience (e.g., QA director versed in FDA regulations). Reviewers expect clear organization of laboratory responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing and data dissemination plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Data from this project will be shared through collaborative publications in the scientific literature, with article repository into the NIH database as well as through national, regional and international conference presentations. Public access to blinded data sets will be provided once analyses and publications are complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concrete plan and timeline for data sharing (NIH repositories, open access publications), capacity-building (e.g., help develop local assay capacity), and stakeholder dissemination. Budget for open-source publication where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium and subcontract roles must be specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Sub-contracts (e.g., with UW and UCD) will support specific tasks: ensuring specimen collection proceeds as planned, monitoring acceptability rates, assisting data management to merge hair level data with parent study data, contributing to analyses, participating in manuscript generation, and liaising with study leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly describe subcontract deliverables, responsibilities, communication plans with parent study leadership, and how subcontractors will support aims (e.g., hair collection logistics, data merging, PK analyses). Include letters of support and budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources (section present; in this application: Not applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if N/A, include a statement addressing authentication; if applicable, describe how key reagents, reference standards, and biological materials will be authenticated and tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT/service level expectations for research support
rubrics_metrics.description: Premium Desktop Support includes defined Hours of Support, Response Times, Hardware and Software support, Storage and Data backup, User Training, Project Management, Presentation Support, and Administrative Rights. ITS goals include assigning and acknowledging ticket assignments within 2 business hours of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document IT support arrangements, expected response times, software availability, remote access, and on-call support for laboratory and presentation needs. Indicate how IT services will support research continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure research computing environment and analytic tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhanced data management systems (MyResearch) provide secure transfer, storage, and analysis of research data via an encrypted portal, with access to statistical applications (SAS, SPSS, Stata), qualitative analysis (Atlas.TI), survey collection (RedCap), and Qualtrics access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe secure computing environments, available analytic software, user training, and any costs for licenses. Explain how these resources meet the project's data analysis and storage requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project-level attachments and document requirements (Project Summary, Narrative, Bibliography, Facilities, Equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, Bibliography & References Cited, Facilities & Other Resources, and Major Equipment attachments are required and listed (e.g., Abstract_R01Rnwl_Gandhi_Final08312016.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required attachments are included, correctly labeled, and meet FOA formatting and page-limit requirements. Provide complete bibliographies and detailed facilities/equipment descriptions.
